lines.text: You pull up to a red light, and somehow it knows you're waiting. Look down. The answer is cut into the road.
Those thin lines in the pavement hide a loop of wire, right under your car.
A box by the road sends alternating current through it, making an invisible magnetic field.
When your car's metal rolls over the loop, tiny currents swirl in the metal and weaken that field.
The box senses the change and tells the signal controller a car is waiting. Your green is on its way.
But a bike has far less metal, so the loop can miss it.
On a bike? Stop with your wheels right over the cut lines, where the loop is most sensitive.
